knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Dirty water belongs in a sluice or utility basin, not on the floor, where it spreads soil and creates a slip hazard.
Bent knees and a secure grip reduce strain; a drain tap removes the need to lift a full bucket.
A bucket stored damp or with residue inside becomes a source of soil and odour for the next job.

practicalCriteria: Empties the bucket at a sluice or utility basin, never onto the floor.
Lifts with bent knees and a secure grip, or uses the drain tap where one is fitted.
Dries and stores the bucket and wringer upright, clear of the floor.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. The practical sign-off is separate, observed by an assessor, and is not shown by a quiz result.
evidenceRequired: Observed practical sign-off on assessor sheet
Equipment check note where the site keeps one
stopWorkCriteria: Dirty water poured on the floor
Full bucket lifted with a bent back by one person
